newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Friday with trading volume thin due to the decreasing fund demand ahead of the weekend, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 9.00 percent from 7.15 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 1.6 million lots from 1.8 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said big institutions traded less ahead of the weekend, making volume thin.
"Most of the repo rates moved narrowly due to the weekend," said one trader. "But a rebound on the domestic A share markets supported the rates for the seven-day and 14-day contracts."
Traders said they believed the repo rates would rise slightly due to a new A share issue on the Shenzhen bourse.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Friday on improved market sentiment with falls on the A share markets in the previous two days pushing some liquidity back to the spot market, traders said.
The contracts had been on a downward trend in the past few weeks with liquidity flowing out to the active stock markets.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 109.42 yuan from 109.25 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 617,837 lots from 785,669 lots.
Traders said the current high yields of the contracts indicated this was a good time to invest in the spot contracts.
They said they believed the spot contracts would continue to rise early next week.
